claims.text: A combined in situ method using high-temperature synchrotron XRD and environmental TEM can simultaneously observe oxidation-scale growth and crystallographic phase transformations.
The combined method provides a more accurate assessment of oxidation kinetics and phase stability than separate measurements.
The initial CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy is as-homogenized.
The initial CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a single-phase solid-solution structure.
CrMnFeCoNi is a high-entropy alloy system relevant to high-temperature oxidation studies.
The proposed measurements are performed at approximately 800–1200°C.
In situ high-temperature XRD can be used on CrMnFeCoNi under an oxidizing air environment.
The relevant structural variables are the evolving surface oxide scale and the underlying crystallographic phases of the alloy.
In situ high-temperature XRD can accurately identify time- and temperature-dependent phase formation or transformation during oxidation.
XRD peak shifts and the emergence of new diffraction peaks can quantify the kinetics of oxide-scale formation.
Environmental TEM concurrently images oxide morphology and alloy microstructural changes during the synchrotron XRD measurement.
Concurrent XRD and environmental TEM observations directly link oxidation behavior to phase transformations.
The combined method will resolve time- and temperature-dependent oxide-scale growth.
The combined method will resolve time- and temperature-dependent phase transformations.
Oxide-scale thickening is expected to correlate with shifts, intensity changes, or appearance and disappearance of diffraction peaks from the underlying alloy.
Temporal and spatial resolution may limit detection of ultrarapid transformations or nanoscale phenomena in very fine microstructures.
The quantitative correlation between oxide growth and phase-transformation kinetics may depend on alloy composition, temperature gradients, and instrument resolution.
